candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate therapeutic medication effects, monitor response, and provide safe medication education.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — fenofibrate and severe hypertriglyceridemia
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize fenofibrate as a triglyceride-lowering option for adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia while avoiding the unsupported claim that treatment guarantees prevention of pancreatitis.

options.A: A substantial reduction in triglyceride-rich lipoproteins; fenofibrate is an evidence-based option for severe hypertriglyceridemia.
options.B: A primary antihypertensive effect with little expected change in triglycerides.
options.C: Selective LDL-C lowering with no clinically meaningful effect on triglycerides.
options.D: Guaranteed prevention of acute pancreatitis once triglycerides begin to fall.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current FDA labeling indicates fenofibrate as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia, defined in the label as triglycerides at least 500 mg/dL. The 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline identifies fibrates as a first-line triglyceride-lowering option in severe hypertriglyceridemia and notes expected triglyceride reductions of roughly 30% to 50%. B and C misstate the primary lipid effect in this scenario. D is too strong: although severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with pancreatitis risk and triglyceride lowering is part of risk management, the fenofibrate label states that its effect on reducing pancreatitis risk has not been determined.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Fenofibrate is indicated and guideline-supported to lower triglycerides in severe hypertriglyceridemia; it should not be described as the only first-line therapy or as guaranteeing prevention of pancreatitis.
candidate.source_document_title: Fenofibrate Tablets Prescribing Information; 2026 ACC/AHA Multisociety Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia
candidate.source_locator: Fenofibrate label, Indications and Usage: adjunct to diet to reduce TG in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia (TG ≥500 mg/dL); limitation notes that the effect of fenofibrate on reducing pancreatitis risk has not been determined. 2026 dyslipidemia guideline, Triglyceride-Lowering Medications/Severe Hypertriglyceridemia: fibrates stimulate PPAR-alpha pathways, generally lower TG about 30%–50%, and are a first-line option for severe hypertriglyceridemia, particularly when TG is ≥500 mg/dL.
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling via DailyMed; American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association and partner societies
candidate.source_version_date: Current fenofibrate label updated through 2025–2026; 2026 dyslipidemia guideline published March 13, 2026; accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: An adult with persistent severe hypertriglyceridemia (fasting triglycerides 620 mg/dL) is prescribed fenofibrate after secondary causes and lifestyle measures are addressed. Which therapeutic effect should the nurse expect?
